主要内容: On February 6, 2012, President Obama signed Executive Order (E.O.) 13599, which implements sanctions under the National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) against Iran. The E.O. freezes all property of the Central Bank of Iran, all other Iranian financial institutions, and the Government of Iran. This action intensifies existing U.S. sanctions on Iran, which have been in place since 1995. Previously, U.S. persons were required to 'reject' Iranian transactions, but under the new E.O., these transactions are now 'blocked,' meaning their assets are frozen. The E.O. emphasizes the U.S. government's resolve to hold Iran accountable for its nuclear program and its failure to meet international obligations. The sanctions are part of a broader effort to increase economic and diplomatic pressure on Iran until it addresses international concerns. On February 6, 2012, President Obama signed Executive Order (E.O.) 13599, which implements sanctions under the National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) against entities owned or controlled by the Government of Iran. These sanctions block transactions involving entities listed on the Treasury Department’s Office of Foreign Assets Control’s (OFAC) SDN List, including those tagged with [IRAN]. U.S. persons are prohibited from engaging in transactions with these entities unless exempt or authorized. OFAC will continue to update the SDN List, adding, deleting, or editing entries as needed. The E.O. does not alter existing sanctions against foreign financial institutions that engage in arms-length transactions with Iranian financial institutions, including the Central Bank of Iran. These institutions remain at risk of U.S. sanctions if they conduct significant financial transactions with the Central Bank of Iran or other designated Iranian financial institutions under the NDAA or the Comprehensive Iran Sanctions, Accountability, and Divestment Act of 2010 (CISADA). Treasury also issued general licenses to maintain existing authorizations for transactions that support U.S. foreign policy interests. OFAC will provide updated guidance on these licenses and the implementation of the E.O. in the near future.
